content.text:
Case A

A1: The seven-day search was only evaluated from 2 hours before publication to now, so it is partial. The earlier requests it found don't cover the full seven days. We can't say the burst was the first misuse, because the search could not see earlier misuse. Cannot tell.

A2: The compromise check scored at 30 minutes using inputs as of 30 minutes. The link between the payout destination and the other two accounts was effective before publication but learned 1 day after. So it was not available to the check at scoring time. The burst at 19 minutes would have been available, but the question asks whether it missed evidence available to it. The shared-destination evidence was not available. The burst itself was available (inputs as of 30 minutes), yet we don't know whether the check used those request features. Still, the record says inputs as of 30 minutes after publication, so the burst data was within scope. Whether the check "missed" it is unclear, since we don't know what it looks at. Cannot tell.

A3: A shared destination alone does not show one owner. No, not by itself.

A4: The outcome channels have no reporting window defined, so absence of reports after 30 days is not informative about legitimacy. Of the offered answers, "No" fits better than "Yes, weakly" because the absence cannot be interpreted. Cannot tell is also plausible, but with no defined window the absence carries no evidential weight, so the answer is No.

A5: The burst involved a different fingerprint, a residential proxy, a payout destination change, and a faster schedule shortly after publication. This warrants investigation. Yes.

Case B

B1: The raw counts show D at 0 recorded, but 2 chargebacks recorded at account X are linked to D's transactions. So D has 2 as well. D's rate is not lower. No.

B2: The combined 5 percent is an aggregate. By account, A and B are 8 percent. So the aggregate doesn't show that no account is above 5 percent. No.

B3: The search was partial and truncated, with sampling at 10 percent on one source. It cannot show there are no other accounts. No.

B4: Both notes link to the agent's cluster assessment, so they are not independent. No.

B5: A blocked payment with no chargeback is not shown to be non-fraud, because the block closed the chargeback channel. No.

B6: Shared templates and descriptor patterns, plus a person tied to A, a closed account, and a rejected application, justify investigating together. Yes.

RESULT MN-040 | A1: Cannot tell | A2: Cannot tell | A3: No, not by itself | A4: No | A5: Yes | B1: No | B2: No | B3: No | B4: No | B5: No | B6: Yes
